title: Pointer Network Stress Test — Run 003 Master Report

s1_high_volume.verdict: Primary strength pointers are highly reliable. Alternative paths degrade quickly.

s2_fanout.verdict: Network well-connected. Even worst scripts reach majority of nodes within 3 hops.

s3_adversarial.verdict: Compact network (diameter 4-5). All SOPs can cycle back. 6 trap patterns identified.

s4_recommendation_load.verdict: Recommendation system is reliable under load. Zero failures across 80 calls.

s5_graph_analysis.verdict: Compact, fully connected network. 124 of 310 nodes are in the center (radius 3).

s6_routing_strategies.verdict: Weight routing is the superior strategy at scale. Tag routing has better coherence but fails to reach targets.

s7_src_accessibility.verdict: Major improvement from repairs. 61.7% vs 36.4% in run-002. Nearly all SRC nodes now accessible.

s8_end_to_end.verdict: Research and discovery workflows excellent. Enrichment and full-stack blocked by wiki isolation and TEAM->SOP gaps.

critical: SCR->wiki connectivity: 100% failure rate in traversals
high: Tag coherence drops to 0 in multi-hop traversals
Enrichment workflows completely broken (can't reach wiki from scripts)
medium: 6 network trap patterns where routing loops
low: No-entry recommendation fallback doesn't consider task context well

improvement_trajectory.run_001: Found critical structural issues — orphans, missing classifications, broken recommendations
improvement_trajectory.run_002: Fixed structural issues — all SOPs tagged, strengths corrected, SRC links added
improvement_trajectory.run_003: Stress tested at scale — confirmed repairs work, identified remaining cross-domain gaps
improvement_trajectory.recommended_run_004: Focus on wiki bridging, TEAM->SOP connectivity, and full-stack workflow enablement
